instruction:
Read docs/TASK_PHASE10.md FIRST (sections 2 and 3). ethsc/rpc.py is in your context: read it, do not modify it. You write ONE NEW file, tests/test_rpc_examples_p10.py; the existing tests/test_rpc_examples.py is not yours and stays byte for byte (it keeps its own tests). It holds the phase-10 examples:

1. RPC Client 6: given the default transport with urllib.request.urlopen replaced by a recorder answering 200 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":"0x1"}; when RpcClient("https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com").call("eth_chainId", []); then the result is "0x1" and the recorded Request has get_header("User-agent") == "ethsc/0.1" and get_header("Content-type") == "application/json" (ref: live 2026-09-30: no User-Agent header gives 403 "error code: 1010", "ethsc/0.1" gives 200)
2. RPC Client 7: given a fake transport answering status 200 with {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":null} twice, then status 200 with the text of tests/fixtures/receipts_26077729.json; prices {"eth_getBlockReceipts": 1000} and an on_spend collector; when call("eth_getBlockReceipts", ["0x18dea21"]); then a list of 218 receipts; 3 transport calls; sleeps [1, 2]; on_spend called once, with ("eth_getBlockReceipts", 1000) (ref: live 2026-09-30: block 20000000 answered null 1 time in 10 requests, a block 3 past the head answered null)
3. RPC Client 8: given a fake transport that always answers 200 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":null}, max_retries=5 and an on_spend collector; when call("eth_getBlockReceipts", ["0x1312d00"]); then RpcError with code None and message "eth_getBlockReceipts returned null" after 6 transport calls; sleeps [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]; on_spend never called
4. RPC Client 9: given a fake transport answering 200 {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":null} once; when call("eth_getCode", ["0xC02aaA39b223FE8D0A0e5C4F27eAD9083C756Cc2", "latest"]); then the result is None after 1 transport call and no sleep (ref: only eth_getBlockReceipts treats null as a failure)
5. RPC Client 10: given the module ethsc.config; when PUBLICNODE_URL is read; then it equals "https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com" and PRICES is unchanged: {"eth_blockNumber": 80, "eth_getBlockReceipts": 1000, "eth_getCode": 80}

Write exactly one test per example above, in the order given, each docstring naming the Function and the example number (e.g. "RPC Client 6"). You are the independent author of the criterion: check what each example says, with the exact numbers it gives, not what the code happens to do. Import every stub from tests/helpers.py (FakeRpc, FakeTransport, CodeServer, FakeUrlopen, InterruptAfter, temp_store, block_codes, block_receipts, load_hex) -- never define your own Fake* class. Offline: no test opens a network connection, and the file imports no network module (replace urlopen with mock.patch and the dotted string "urllib.request.urlopen"). Every --db, report prefix or other file a test writes goes into a tempfile.mkdtemp() directory, never the working directory. unittest, msg= on every assert, Python 3.9 syntax, standard library only. Keep the file short: one scenario per test, short docstrings.

Read docs/TASK_PHASE10.md FIRST (sections 2 and 3). ethsc/cli.py is in your context: read it, do not modify it. You write ONE NEW file, tests/test_cli_examples_p10.py; the existing tests/test_cli_examples.py is not yours and stays byte for byte (it keeps its own tests). It holds the phase-10 examples:

1. Command Line 21: given INFURA_API_KEY unset, no .env, a fresh db and the fake rpc over block 26077729 (receipts_26077729.json, codes_26077729.json); when main(["--db", db, "backfill", "--from", "26077729", "--to", "26077729", "--source", "publicnode"], rpc=fake); then exit 0, stdout and stderr empty, the db holds 206 addresses and 130 codes, every eth_getCode call carries "latest" as its second param, and spent of today (UTC) is 0 (ref: phase 10: the public node, keyless and not an archive node)
2. Command Line 22: given a fresh db and the same fake rpc; when the same backfill without --source; then exit 0, the db holds 206 addresses and 130 codes, every eth_getCode call carries "0x18dea21" as its second param, and spent of today (UTC) is 17560 (ref: Infura stays the default and unchanged: 80 + 1000 + 206 × 80)
3. Command Line 23: given ethsc.cli.follow_chain replaced by a recorder returning {"blocks": 0, "stopped": None, "progress": None, "alerts": [], "day": "2026-09-30"}, and a fake rpc; when backfill --from 26077729 --to 26077729 is run with no source flag, with --source publicnode, and with --source publicnode --workers 3; then exit 0 each time; the recorded keyword arguments are workers 1, code_tag None, prices equal to ethsc.config.PRICES; then workers 8, code_tag "latest", prices {}; then workers 3, code_tag "latest", prices {}
4. Command Line 24: given INFURA_API_KEY unset, no .env, ethsc.cli.RpcClient replaced by a recorder that returns a fake rpc over block 26077729, and ethsc.cli.infura_url replaced by one that raises AssertionError; when main(["--db", db, "backfill", "--from", "26077729", "--to", "26077729", "--source", "publicnode"]) is run with rpc=None; then exit 0; RpcClient was constructed once, with the url "https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com", prices {} and max_retries 5; infura_url was never called
5. Command Line 25: given a fresh db and a fake rpc; when main(["--db", db, "backfill", "--from", "26077729", "--to", "26077729", "--source", "publicnode", "--daily-budget", "3000000"], rpc=fake) and the same with listen instead of backfill --from/--to; then exit 2 both times, stdout empty, stderr exactly one line, and the fake rpc recorded no call (ref: the daily budget is an Infura credit budget; refused, not ignored)
6. Command Line 26: given a fresh db and a fake rpc; when main with backfill --from 26077729 --to 26077729 and --workers 0, then with --source alchemy; then exit 2 both times, stdout empty, stderr exactly one line, and the fake rpc recorded no call
7. Command Line 27: given a db with progress 26077728 and a fake rpc answering eth_blockNumber "0x18dea21" and eth_getBlockReceipts null; when main(["--db", db, "listen", "--source", "publicnode"], rpc=fake, sleep=fake_sleep); then exit 1, stdout empty, stderr exactly one line containing "eth_getBlockReceipts returned null", no traceback, progress still 26077728, sleep never called (ref: decision 2026-09-30: no new semantics for a null that outlived the retries; exit 1 as for any RpcError)
